div.p: We maintain four repeaters that are open and free for all licensed radio amateurs to use. They cover much of Sonoma County plus parts of Marin, Napa, and Lake Counties, and even reach into the East Bay. We also maintain a Winlink packet gateway and an IRLP node - see the repeater policy for usage guidelines.

ul.li: 147.315 + PL 88.5 (Analog FM, VHF) - our most-used repeater, located southwest of Sebastopol on English Hill.
224.480 - PL 88.5 (Analog FM, VHF) - the 1.25m repeater on English Hill, open to all despite minimal use.
441.375 + PL 88.5 (Analog FM/YSF, UHF) - set your analog radio's receive tone to PL 88.5 to avoid YSF digital noise. Located in eastern Santa Rosa.
443.100 + CC1 (DMR, UHF) - located on English Hill; see the DMR page for details.
Ragchew Net - Mondays 8pm, English Hill repeater - a moderated conversational net for radio topics, station setup, hobbies, and travels.
Service Net - Tuesdays 7pm, English Hill repeater - club news, Newsline, and radio equipment checks.
DMR Net - Thursdays 6:30pm, DMR repeater - open to any amateur operator with DMR capability.
Fusion Net - Thursdays 7:00pm, YSF repeater - practice using Fusion and connect with other enthusiasts of this mode.

div.p: Winlink Packet System - Gateway callsign W6SON-10, frequency 144.910 MHz, Packet/1200, located on English Hill, digipeater W6SON-1. Currently testing two additional gateways: W6SON-10 (packet, 146.580, NE Santa Rosa) and W6SON-11 (VARA FM, 441.500, Cotati) - reports welcome to repeater@sonomacountyradioamateurs.com.
IRLP - Node 7103, frequency 147.315 + PL 88.5, located on English Hill. See the IRLP page for details.

SCRA has a UHF (70cm) DMR repeater in service on English Hill in West Sonoma County. Coverage extends from Sebastopol and nearly all of Santa Rosa, Windsor, and Rohnert Park/Cotati. Thanks go to the Repeater Committee and particularly Curt WA6TIP for spearheading the repeater's provisioning.
Every Thursday night at 6:30pm Pacific Time, Randy AA6RH runs the Sonoma County DMR Net on the BrandMeister network, talk group 31707 (Sonoma County). Open to anyone with DMR-capable equipment.
One static talk group operates full-time: Sonoma County talk group 31707.

div.p: More info: DMR Is Easy (getting started) and DMR Code Plugs (ready-made configurations).

DMR provides an excellent opportunity to communicate with amateur radio operators worldwide with ease. It can also facilitate coordination of traditional point-to-point RF contacts without requiring DX clusters or similar tools.

ol.li: Obtain a DMR ID by visiting RadioID. Register for an account, verify your amateur licence, and receive an ID number to program into your radio. Processing can take up to 24 hours, so registering before your radio arrives is worthwhile.

Purchase a DMR radio, handheld or mobile. Budget-friendly options from China start around $65; mobile radios begin near $300, with premium brands (Motorola, Kenwood, Hytera) costing significantly more.

div.p: Randy AA6RH delivered a presentation to the club during its January 2019 Member Meeting covering DMR fundamentals.
SCRA provides beginner-friendly DMR code plugs for several popular radio models. These configurations include local repeaters and curated talk groups for Northern California operators.
Important: get your own DMR ID before using these code plugs - they contain an invalid placeholder ID by default. Register at radioid.net.

div.p: To connect to IRLP Node 9250 (Western Reflector): identify yourself, observe the recommended wait times, then disconnect using DTMF codes 7-3.
The SCRA repeater system is available for appropriate use by duly licensed radio amateurs and groups.

Usage follows this hierarchy: emergency communications, SCRA-approved directed nets, SCRA member usage, and non-SCRA related usage. Those seeking to use the system in ways not currently sanctioned should contact SCRA.

ul.li: Follow Good Amateur Practice - exercise courtesy and common sense.
Station Identification - identify your station call sign appropriately every ten minutes and at the end of a conversation.
Testing Protocol - "kerchunking" without identification is prohibited; testing should include clear identification and "clear" when finished.
Language Standards - no obscene, indecent, or profane language is tolerated.
Broadcasting Prohibited - no broadcasting is allowed on the system.

Operating Procedure - listen before transmitting, hold PTT briefly before speaking, state the called station's callsign first followed by yours, and avoid codes, Q-words, and excessive phonetics unless requested.
Topic Guidelines - avoid controversial subjects, such as politics, religion, or criticisms of other amateurs or ham radio groups.

div.p: Non-compliance may result in formal denial of repeater access. The repeater trustee or control operators will shut off the repeater should a warning of unauthorized or inappropriate use go unheeded.
Frequent users are encouraged to become active SCRA members to help support maintenance and improvements.
